title: Ethiopian Chemistry University Entrance Exam 2015
description: Ethiopian Chemistry University Entrance Exam 2015 featuring 79 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the main reason for the large difference in dipole-moment between the triatomic molecules water (H₂O) and carbon dioxide (CO₂)?
options: The presence of multiple bonds in carbon dioxide (CO₂) while single bonds in water .
The bonds in carbon dioxide (CO₂) are directed 180° and bond polarity reinforces each other.
The presence of lone pairs of electrons in water (H₂O) partially reinforces bond polarities.
The higher electronegativity difference among atoms in water (H₂O) than in carbon dioxide (CO₂).
questions.explanation:
Water (H₂O) has a bent molecular shape due to the presence of two lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom.

 This bent geometry causes the individual O–H bond dipoles to partially reinforce each other, resulting in a significant net dipole moment.

 In contrast, carbon dioxide (CO₂) is linear with bond angles of 180°, so the C=O bond dipoles cancel each other, giving CO₂ a zero net dipole moment.

questions.questionText: How many non-bonding pairs of electrons are present in the valence shell of the central atom in ClF₃?
questions.explanation:
In ClF₃, chlorine is the central atom with 7 valence electrons. 

Three electrons are used to form three Cl–F bonds, leaving four electrons unshared.

 These four electrons form two non-bonding (lone) pairs. According to VSEPR theory, this results in a T-shaped molecular geometry.

questions.questionText: Which one would be observed in a laboratory activity that is applied on naphthalene?
options: It shows relatively high melting point.
It conducts electricity in molten state.
questions.explanation:
Naphthalene is a non-polar covalent organic compound. 

According to the principle 'like dissolves like', non-polar substances dissolve in non-polar solvents such as benzene.

 Naphthalene is insoluble in water, has a relatively low melting point compared to ionic solids, and does not conduct electricity in either solid or molten state.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
options: In Lewis model, electrons repel one another and a pair of bonding electrons lies far apart as possible.
Valence-bond model explain molecular shape from the interaction of atomic orbitals.
Valence bond model simply shows the linkage between atoms and the presence of lone pairs.
Lewis model predicts the shapes of molecules based on electron-pair repulsions around a central atom.
questions.explanation:
The valence-bond model explains molecular shape by considering the overlap and interaction of atomic orbitals, often through hybridization.

 The Lewis model mainly shows electron distribution and bonding but does not accurately predict molecular shapes based on electron-pair repulsions—that role belongs to VSEPR theory.

questions.questionText: The energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into gaseous ions is called:
questions.explanation:
Lattice energy is the energy required to completely separate one mole of an ionic solid into its constituent gaseous ions.

 It is a measure of the strength of the electrostatic forces holding the ions together in the crystal lattice.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following IS TRUE about isotopes?
options: Isotopes of the same elements contain the same number of neutrons.
Isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties.
Isotopes of an element are atoms that have different number of electrons and protons.
Isotopes of an element are identical in mass number.
questions.explanation:
Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

 Since chemical properties depend on the number of protons (and thus electrons), isotopes of an element exhibit the same chemical behavior even though their masses differ.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following describes the quantum mechanical model?
options: An atom is a sphere with a positively charged matter, in which electrons are embedded.
Electrons moved around the nucleus of an atom in circular orbits.
The locations of electrons in an atom are described in terms of probability.
An atom is represented by a solid indestructible sphere.
questions.explanation:
The quantum mechanical model of the atom describes electrons as existing in regions of space called orbitals, where the probability of finding an electron is highest.

 Earlier models, such as the Thomson model, Rutherford model, and Bohr model, do not accurately describe the probabilistic nature of electron positions.

questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an ionic compound?
questions.explanation:
CaCl₂ (calcium chloride) is an ionic compound formed from a metal (calcium) and a non-metal (chlorine).

 The other options are covalent compounds: PCl₃ (phosphorus trichloride), H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide), and CO₂ (carbon dioxide) consist of non-metal atoms sharing electrons.

questions.questionText: An element is located in Group VIIA and 3 rd period of the modern periodic table. On the basis of this the element:
options: generally forms an ion with -2 charges.
questions.explanation:
An element in Group VIIA (the halogens) and 3rd period is chlorine (Cl).

 Halogens generally form acidic oxides (e.g., Cl₂O, Cl₂O₃, Cl₂O₇). 

They have high electron affinity, typically form ions with -1 charge, and have high ionization energy, not very low.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a colorless, flammable volatile liquid and miscible with non-polar solvents?
questions.explanation:
Benzene is a colorless, flammable, volatile liquid that is non-polar and miscible with other non-polar solvents.

 Methanol and ethanol are polar and miscible with water, while methane is a gas at room temperature.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following petroleum products is used as a solvent and in dry cleaning?
questions.explanation:
Petroleum ether is a light hydrocarbon fraction obtained from petroleum.

 It is highly volatile, non-polar, and used as a solvent in laboratories and in dry cleaning. 

The other options have different uses: paraffin wax is for candles, diesel oil as fuel, and kerosene as fuel and heating oil.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is NOT TRUE about laboratory preparation of ethylene by dehydration of ethanol?
options: Combustion of ethylene produces a non-luminous flame.
The collected ethylene gas in the experiment decolorizes alkaline KMnO₄.
The collected ethylene gas in the experiment decolorizes Br₂ in CCl₄.
Concentrated sulphuric acid is used as a dehydrating agent.
questions.explanation:
Ethylene (C₂H₄) is an unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene) that reacts with bromine water (Br₂ in CCl₄) and decolorizes it. 

However, in the laboratory preparation of ethylene, the collected gas is usually not strong enough to decolorize alkaline KMnO₄ immediately. 

Concentrated H₂SO₄ acts as the dehydrating agent, and combustion of ethylene gives a non-luminous flame due to its clean burning.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an essential nutrient of plants?
questions.explanation:
Potassium (K) is an essential macronutrient for plants. 

It regulates osmotic balance, activates enzymes, and is important for photosynthesis and growth.

 Sodium, aluminum, and lead are not essential; lead is toxic, aluminum can be toxic at high concentrations, and sodium is only essential for some plants in trace amounts.

questions.questionText: The heat change at constant pressure that results when 1 mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states is:
questions.explanation:
The standard enthalpy of formation (ΔH⁰f) is defined as the heat change that occurs when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states under standard conditions (1 atm, 25°C).

 Other options refer to different thermodynamic quantities: standard reduction potential measures the tendency of a species to be reduced, standard entropy of reaction is related to disorder change, and standard enthalpy of reaction is the overall enthalpy change for a reaction.

questions.questionText: What is a redox reaction? It is a reaction in which
options: atoms or ions of two compound exchange bonding partners.
an acid and a base neutralize each other.
two insoluble ions in compounds form an insoluble products.
questions.explanation:
A redox (reduction-oxidation) reaction is one in which electrons are transferred from one species to another.

 Oxidation involves the loss of electrons, while reduction involves the gain of electrons.

 The other options describe double displacement reactions, neutralization reactions, or precipitation reactions, which are not necessarily redox processes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains how electroplating takes place?
options: The cations in the electrolyte are supplied either by the added salt or from oxidation of the anode.
Metal is deposited on the anode by reduction of ions in the electrolyte solution.
The electrolyte is an aqueous solution of a salt of the plated metal.
The object to be electroplated either metal or graphite-coated plastic constitutes the anode.
questions.explanation:
In electroplating, the metal to be plated is deposited on the cathode.

 The cations of the plating metal are present in the electrolyte and are supplied either by the dissolved salt or by oxidation of the anode (if it is made of the plating metal).

 The object to be plated serves as the cathode, not the anode.

questions.questionText: How does the equivalent mass of a base is obtained?
options: By multiplying its number of equivalent by the number of OH⁻ ions furnished by one formula unit of a base.
By dividing its number of equivalent by the number of OH⁻ ions furnished by one formula unit of a base.
By multiplying its molar mass by the number of OH⁻ ions furnished by one formula unit of a base.
By dividing its molar mass by the number of OH⁻ ions furnished by one formula unit of a base.
questions.explanation:
The equivalent mass of a base is calculated by dividing its molar mass by the number of hydroxide ions (OH⁻) that one formula unit of the base can furnish.

 For example, for NaOH, which furnishes one OH⁻, the equivalent mass equals its molar mass; for Ca(OH)₂, which furnishes two OH⁻, the equivalent mass is half of its molar mass.

questions.questionText: Which of the following compounds reacts with basic oxide to form salt and water?
questions.explanation:
Acids react with basic oxides (metal oxides) in a neutralization reaction to produce a salt and water. For example, HCl reacts with CaO to form CaCl₂ and H₂O. 

Bases do not react with basic oxides, neutral oxides are generally inert, and acidic oxides react with bases, not with other basic oxides.

questions.questionText: The negative logarithm of the molar concentration of hydrogen ion to the base ten is known as
questions.explanation:
The pH of a solution is defined as the negative logarithm (base 10) of the hydrogen ion concentration: pH = -log₁₀[H⁺].

 Kₐ is the acid dissociation constant, 

- pOH measures hydroxide ion concentration, 

- K_w is the ionization constant of water.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following galvanic cell is an example of secondary cell?
questions.explanation:
A secondary cell is a rechargeable galvanic cell. The lead storage cell (lead-acid battery) can be recharged by passing current in the reverse direction.

 Leclanché, zinc-carbon, and Daniel's cells are primary cells, which cannot be recharged once the reactants are exhausted.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is responsible for electrolyte conductivity?
options: Ions strongly held in a fixed position.
questions.explanation:
The conductivity of an electrolyte is due to the movement of ions in the solution.

 Positive ions (cations) move toward the cathode, and negative ions (anions) move toward the anode, allowing electric current to flow.

 Electrons held in a fixed position or free electrons in metals do not contribute to electrolyte conductivity.

questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Carbon forms two stable compounds with oxygen, namely, carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide. For a fixed mass of carbon, the ratio of oxygen in carbon monoxide to oxygen in carbon dioxide is 1:2. This result is consistent with the law of
questions.explanation:
The Law of Multiple Proportions states that when two elements form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in ratios of small whole numbers.

 Here, for a fixed mass of carbon, the ratio of oxygen in CO to CO₂ is 1:2, which exemplifies this law.

questions.questionText: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed by a change of variable, the system shifts the equilibrium position in a way that tends to counteract this change of variable. This is a statement for
questions.explanation:
Le Chatelier's Principle states that if a system at equilibrium is subjected to a change in concentration, temperature, or pressure, the system will adjust itself to partially counteract the effect of the disturbance and restore equilibrium. 

The other options refer to quantum mechanics and electron configuration rules.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following graphs illustrates the rate change in terms of change in reactant concentration with time?
options: Graph A (Concentration starts high, decreases rapidly then slows)
Graph B (Concentration starts low, increases rapidly then slows)
Graph C (Concentration starts high, increases slowly)
Graph D (Concentration starts low, decreases slowly)
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following gas laws states the volume of a fixed amount of gas maintained at constant pressure is directly proportional to the absolute temperature of the gas?
questions.explanation:
Charles' Law states that for a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure, the volume is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (V ∝ T). 

Boyle's Law relates pressure and volume at constant temperature, Avogadro's Law relates volume and number of moles, and the Combined Gas Law combines Boyle's, Charles', and Gay-Lussac's laws.

questions.questionText: Which of the following would occur during the formation of ions?
options: The electronic configuration of an atom forming the ion remains unaffected.
Valence electrons are transferred from one atom to another.
Inner most shell electrons are involved.
Valence electrons are shared between atoms.
questions.explanation:
During the formation of ions, atoms gain or lose electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration, usually that of a noble gas.

 This involves the transfer of valence electrons from one atom to another. 

Inner electrons are generally not involved, and sharing of electrons occurs in covalent bonding, not ionic formation.

questions.questionText: In order to illustrate the structure and properties of a solid, a student put simple space network and around the nodes representing metal cations, he filled the remaining space between the marbles with electrons. Which one of the following bonding is represented by this model?
questions.explanation:
The model described represents metallic bonding, where metal cations are arranged in a lattice and the valence electrons are delocalized, moving freely throughout the structure.

 This 'sea of electrons' explains properties such as electrical conductivity, malleability, and ductility. 

Covalent bonding involves sharing electrons between specific atoms, ionic bonding involves transfer of electrons, and dative bonding involves a shared pair of electrons from one atom.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains dipole-dipole force?
options: An attractive force resulting from temporary dipoles induced in molecules.
An electrostatic attraction between metal ions and valence electrons.
type of intermolecular force that exists between non-polar molecules.
The intermolecular attraction between oppositely charged poles of nearby polar molecules.
questions.explanation:
Dipole-dipole forces are intermolecular attractions that occur between polar molecules, where the positive end of one molecule is attracted to the negative end of another.

 The first option describes London dispersion forces, the second describes metallic bonding, and the third describes forces between non-polar molecules (also London forces).

questions.questionText: A reaction that involves the exchange of positive and negative ions of each reactant is a definition of a
questions.explanation: A double displacement reaction involves the exchange of positive and negative ions between two compounds to form new compounds. For example, AB + CD → AD + CB. Single displacement involves one element replacing another, decomposition breaks a compound into simpler substances, and combination reactions form a single product from two or more reactants.

questions.questionText: In a kinetic experiment, a student placed crystals of iodine in a closed reaction vessel, introduced a given quantity of hydrogen gas, and collected data to calculate the rate of formation of hydrogen iodide. What would be the effect observed on the rate of the reaction if the student takes twice the amount of iodine from that used in the first experiment?
options: The formation of hydrogen iodide will be decreased.
The rate of the reaction will be constant.
It speeds up the rate of the reaction.
It lowers the rate of the reaction.
questions.explanation:
The rate of a chemical reaction generally increases with the concentration of reactants. 

In the reaction H₂ + I₂ → 2HI, increasing the amount of iodine increases its concentration, leading to a higher collision frequency between H₂ and I₂ molecules, thereby speeding up the rate of formation of hydrogen iodide.

questions.questionText: Which of the following CORRECTLY relates the vapor pressure of a liquid with its boiling point? Boiling point is
options: the temperature at which molecules present in the vapor phase go back to the liquid state.
the temperature at which the kinetic energy of molecules is much less than the intermolecular force.
the temperature at which all the three physical state co-exist.
the temperature at which the vapor pressure becomes equal to the external pressure.
questions.explanation:
The boiling point of a liquid is defined as the temperature at which its vapor pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure, allowing bubbles of vapor to form within the liquid.

 The first option describes condensation, the second is incorrect regarding energy comparison, and the third describes the triple point, not boiling.

questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following results from interaction of the atomic orbitals of bonding atoms to produce new electron distribution associated with the entire molecule?
questions.explanation:
Molecular orbitals are formed when atomic orbitals from bonding atoms combine, producing new orbitals that extend over the entire molecule.

 These orbitals describe the probability distribution of electrons in the molecule.

 Hybrid orbitals result from mixing atomic orbitals on the same atom, not over the entire molecule

questions.questionText: Which type of organic substances would be produced by heating a mixture of a carboxylic acid and an alcohol in the presence of H2SO4?
questions.explanation:
When a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄ (which acts as a dehydrating agent), an ester is formed in a reaction known as esterification.

 Esters of glycerol and fatty acids are fats and oils. Ethers, ketones, and aldehydes are formed through different reactions.

questions.questionText: Which of the properties of solvents WOULD NOT be affected by the formation of a solution with a non-volatile solute?
questions.explanation:
The chemical identity of the solvent does not change when a non-volatile solute is dissolved; it remains chemically the same substance. 

However, colligative properties such as freezing point, boiling point, and chemical potential are affected because they depend on the number of solute particles in the solution.

questions.questionText: The partial pressure of acetylene, C2H2, in a container is 10 atm at 25 °C. What is the solubility in molarity of C2H2, assume that C2H2 obeys Henry's law? (K_H = 1.04 mol/L atm)
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: What is the normality of a solution that contains 19.6 g of H₂SO₄ in 20 mL of the solution?
questions.explanation:
Normality (N) = equivalents of solute / liters of solution.

1. Molar mass of H₂SO₄ = 98 g/mol.  

2. Number of moles = 19.6 g / 98 g/mol = 0.2 mol.  

3. Each H₂SO₄ molecule can furnish 2 H⁺ ions, so equivalents = 0.2 × 2 = 0.4 eq.  

4. Volume of solution = 20 mL = 0.02 L.  

5. Normality = 0.4 eq / 0.02 L = 20 N.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following illustrates an extensive property?
options: Doubling the volume of a sample also doubles the mass; so the ratio of mass to volume remains the same.
If water in two beakers at the same temperature are mixed to make a single quantity of water and the temperature of the combined quantity of water is the same as it was in the two separate beakers.
The electrode potential at standard condition for the half-reaction Cu2+ + 2e- --> Cu is the same as for 2Cu²+ + 4e- --> 2Cu.
If a system is divided into parts and it is found that the property of the complete system has a value that is the sum of the values of the property of all the parts.
questions.explanation: An extensive property is a physical quantity whose value is proportional to the amount of substance (e.g., mass, volume, total energy).

questions.questionText: Which of the following would occur during the formation of ions?
options: The electronic configuration of an atom forming the ion remains unaffected.
Valence electrons are transferred from one atom to another.
Inner most shell electrons are involved.
Valence electrons are shared between atoms.
questions.explanation:
During the formation of ions, atoms gain or lose electrons to achieve a stable electronic configuration, usually that of a noble gas.

 This involves the transfer of valence electrons from one atom to another. 

Inner electrons are generally not involved, and sharing of electrons occurs in covalent bonding, not ionic formation.

questions.questionText: The point in a titration at which the number of moles of OH⁻ ions added to a solution is equal to the number of moles of H⁺ ions originally present is
questions.explanation:
The equivalence point in a titration is reached when the amount of titrant added is stoichiometrically equal to the amount of analyte present in the solution.

 For an acid-base titration, this is the point where moles of OH⁻ added equal the moles of H⁺ in the solution.

 The end point is indicated by a color change of an indicator, triple point refers to a physical state phenomenon, and zero point is not relevant here.

questions.questionText: The speed with which a solute goes into solution is
questions.explanation:
The rate of dissolution refers to how fast a solute dissolves in a solvent. 

Extent of dissolution refers to how much solute can dissolve, degree of solvation refers to how well solvent molecules surround solute particles, and heat of solution is the energy change during dissolution.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains how 2 L of 1 M NaOH aqueous stock solution is converted into a 0.25 M NaOH solution?
options: Evaporating 0.25 L of water from the stock solution
Evaporating 1 L of water from the stock solution
Adding 6 L water to the stock solution
Adding 8 L water to the stock solution
questions.explanation:
To dilute a solution, the dilution formula M₁V₁ = M₂V₂ is used:

M₁ = 1 M, V₁ = 2 L, M₂ = 0.25 M

V₂ = (M₁ × V₁) / M₂ = (1 × 2) / 0.25 = 8 L total solution.

Since we already have 2 L, we need to add 8 - 2 = 6 L of water to achieve 0.25 M NaOH.

questions.questionText: The pH of a 0.1M solution of formic acid (HCOOH) is 3. What is the Ka of the acid?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: A system does 15 J of work and no other changes take place. Which of the following function has fallen by 15 J?
questions.explanation:
According to the first law of thermodynamics, the change in internal energy (ΔU) of a system is equal to the heat added to the system minus the work done by the system.

 Here, no heat is exchanged (Q = 0), and the system does 15 J of work (W = 15 J), so ΔU = Q - W = 0 - 15 = -15 J. 

Enthalpy depends on internal energy and pressure-volume work, entropy measures disorder, and specific heat is a property, not an energy function.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is CORRECTLY stated about the spontaneity of a reaction?
options: For an endothermic reaction with positive reaction entropy, the reaction is non-spontaneous at low temperature.
For an exothermic reaction with negative reaction entropy, the reaction is spontaneous at high temperature.
For an exothermic reaction with negative reaction entropy, the reaction is spontaneous at all temperature.
For an exothermic reaction with positive reaction entropy, the reaction is non-spontaneous at all temperature.
questions.explanation:
The spontaneity of a reaction is determined by Gibbs free energy: ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. 

- For an endothermic reaction (ΔH > 0) with positive entropy change (ΔS > 0), ΔG = ΔH - TΔS. At low T, TΔS is small, so ΔG > 0 → non-spontaneous; at high T, TΔS may exceed ΔH, making ΔG < 0 → spontaneous.

- Exothermic reactions with negative ΔS may only be spontaneous at low temperatures, not all temperatures.

questions.questionText: In thermodynamics, solutions in a beaker, a gas in a cylinder, a reaction vessel, a biological cell are examples of a
questions.explanation:
A thermodynamic system is a defined portion of matter or space under study, separated from its surroundings by a boundary.

 Examples include solutions in a beaker, a gas in a cylinder, a reaction vessel, or a biological cell. Path functions depend on the process (like work or heat), and state functions depend only on the state of the system (like internal energy, enthalpy).

 Thermodynamic variables describe properties of the system.

questions.questionText: What are the four quantum numbers for an electron in a 2s orbital?
questions.explanation:
The four quantum numbers are:

- Principal quantum number (n) = 2 (for the second shell)

- Azimuthal quantum number (l) = 0 (for s-orbital)

- Magnetic quantum number (mₗ) = 0 (since l = 0)

- Spin quantum number (mₛ) = +1/2 (one of the two possible spin states).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is TRUE about gases?
options: When a gas sample is heated at constant pressure, its volume decreases.
The volume of a gas is equal to the volume of its container.
The particles of gases are close to each other.
The volume of a gas is kept constant as pressure increases.
questions.explanation:
Gases have no fixed shape or volume and expand to completely fill their container.

 Heating at constant pressure increases volume (Charles’ Law), gas particles are far apart, and the volume changes when pressure changes (Boyle’s Law).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following mathematical expressions is derived from the combination of Boyle's law, Charles' law and Avogadro's law?
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText:
180 g of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) is allowed to react with 156 gram of hydrochloric acid (HCl), according to the following reaction. Which of the following substances is the limiting reagent? (Atomic masses: Ca=40, Cl=35.5, O=16, C=12, H=1)
CaCO3 + 2HCl --> CaCl2 + CO2 + H2O
questions.explanation: Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following isomers differs in the arrangement of carbon atoms in the longest continuous carbon chain?
questions.explanation:
Structural isomers (also called constitutional isomers) differ in the connectivity of atoms, including the arrangement of the carbon skeleton. 

Cis-trans (geometric) isomers differ in the spatial orientation around a double bond, and position isomers differ in the position of a functional group on the same carbon chain.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following methods can be used in the laboratory for the preparation of alkynes?
options: Dehydrohalogenation of adjacent dihalides with sodium hydroxide.
Hydrogenation of alkenes with a metal catalyst.
Dehydration of alcohols with concentrated sulphuric acid.
Heating of sodium salt of an organic acid with soda lime.
questions.explanation:
Alkynes can be prepared in the laboratory by dehydrohalogenation of vicinal (adjacent) dihalides using a strong base such as alcoholic NaOH, which removes two hydrogen halide molecules.

 Hydrogenation of alkenes gives alkanes, dehydration of alcohols gives alkenes, and heating sodium salts with soda lime produces alkanes (decarboxylation).

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is TRUE about the electrolysis of a molten hypothetical electrolyte, MX?
options: Electrons are not transferred from one species to the other.
The overall reaction is redox reaction.
X is produced at the negative electrode.
M is produced at the anode.
questions.explanation: Electrolysis of a molten electrolyte involves the transfer of electrons: cations gain electrons at the cathode (reduction) and anions lose electrons at the anode (oxidation). This makes the overall process a redox reaction. In molten MX, M⁺ is reduced at the cathode (negative electrode) to form M, and X⁻ is oxidized at the anode (positive electrode) to form X. Therefore, options 3 and 4 are incorrect.

questions.questionText: During the extraction of an unknown metal, the metallic ore was fused with NaOH in air and then dissolved in water to obtain the soluble unknown metal containing species. Reduction with carbon is followed after the solution is treated with HCl. Finally, the obtained oxide is reduced to its metallic form by aluminum. The most probable unknown metal would be
questions.explanation:
Zinc is extracted from its ore (usually ZnO) by fusion with NaOH to form soluble zincate (Na₂[Zn(OH)₄]), which can be dissolved in water. 

Treatment with HCl produces Zn(OH)₂, which upon heating forms ZnO. 
The ZnO is finally reduced to metallic zinc by aluminum in a thermite-like reaction.

 Cu and Pb ores are treated differently, and Ca is highly reactive and extracted by electrolysis, not by this method.

questions.questionText: Why tin does NOT react with cold water but calcium reacts with cold water quite readily?
options: Due to the pH of water.
Due to its less reactive nature.
Due to the formation of a thin oxide layer.
questions.explanation:
Calcium is an active metal and reacts readily with cold water to form calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

 Tin is much less reactive, so it does not react appreciably with cold water under normal conditions.

 The formation of a thin oxide layer may slightly protect some metals, but the primary reason for tin's lack of reaction is its low reactivity.

questions.questionText: Why is vulcanization performed in natural rubber?
options: To decrease the number of monomer unit in the natural rubber.
To increase the number of monomer unit in the natural rubber.
To convert the monomer unit in natural rubber in to polymer.
To establish cross-links between polymer chain in the natural rubber.
questions.explanation:
Vulcanization is the process of heating natural rubber with sulfur to form cross-links (sulfur bridges) between polymer chains.

 This improves elasticity, strength, and durability. 
It does not change the number of monomer units or convert monomers into polymers, as natural rubber is already a polymer.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains the determination of the cell potential of Zn-Cu using voltmeter?
options: U-tube served as a salt bridge that can be filled with saturated KCl.
After the experiment the mass of zinc is increased.
In the Cu half-cell, Cu metal will be dipped in ZnSO₄ solution.
In the Zn half-cell, Zn metal will be dipped in CuSO₄ solution.
questions.explanation:
In a Zn-Cu galvanic cell, the Zn electrode is placed in ZnSO₄ solution, and the Cu electrode is placed in CuSO₄ solution.

 A salt bridge, often a U-tube filled with saturated KCl or another inert electrolyte, completes the circuit and allows ion flow to maintain charge balance.

 The other options are incorrect arrangements of electrodes or misstatements of mass changes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements describes chemical industries? It is
options: process in which dissolved solute comes out of solution and forms crystals.
firm that involves usage of raw material to produce desired products by using chemical reactions and refining methods.
An area of chemistry concerned with the speeds, or rates, at which chemical reactions occur.
An expression for the chemical composition of a compound in terms of the symbols of the atoms of the elements involved.
questions.explanation:
Chemical industries are firms or companies that take raw materials and convert them into useful products through chemical reactions, processes, and refining techniques. 

The other options describe crystallization, chemical kinetics, and chemical formulas, which are not definitions of chemical industries.

questions.questionText: What will be the product if phosphorus reacts with excess amount of oxygen?
questions.explanation:
When phosphorus (P₄) reacts with excess oxygen, it forms tetraphosphorus decoxide (P₄O₁₀).

 If the amount of oxygen is limited, tetraphosphorus hexoxide (P₄O₆) is formed. 

H₃PO₃ and H₃PO₄ are acids that can be formed by dissolving these oxides in water, not by direct reaction of phosphorus with oxygen.

questions.questionText: One of the basic differences between metallic conduction and electrolytic conduction is:
options: The charge carriers in metals are localized electrons while strongly held ions are in electrolytic conduction.
The conduction of electricity is due to the movement of ions in metallic conduction while the flow of mobile electrons in electrolytic conduction.
The conduction of electricity is due to the movement of ions in an electrolytic conduction while the flow of mobile electrons in metallic conduction.
The charge carriers in metals are cations and anions while mobile electrons are in electrolytic conduction.
questions.explanation:
In metallic conduction, electricity is carried by free (delocalized) electrons moving through the metal lattice. 

In electrolytic conduction, the flow of electric current is due to the movement of ions in the electrolyte solution. 

This is the fundamental difference between the two types of conduction.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following gases is released from combustion of a fuel in an industrial machinery causing global warming?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is the primary greenhouse gas released during the combustion of carbon-containing fuels in industrial machinery, vehicles, and power plants. CO₂ traps heat in the atmosphere, contributing to global warming. NO and SO₂ contribute to acid rain and air pollution, while CO is a toxic gas but not a significant greenhouse gas.

questions.questionText: The number of digits to the right of the decimal point denotes:
questions.explanation:
Decimal places refer to the number of digits written to the right of the decimal point in a number.

 Significant figures indicate the total number of meaningful digits in a number, scientific notation expresses numbers in the form of a × 10ⁿ, and conversion factor is used to convert units.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of molecular crystals?
questions.explanation:
Molecular crystals are composed of molecules held together by weak intermolecular forces such as Van der Waals forces or hydrogen bonds.

 Solid CO₂ (dry ice) is an example, where CO₂ molecules form a crystalline lattice. 

Magnesium is a metallic crystal, diamond is a covalent network crystal, and NaCl is an ionic crystal.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following **COULD NOT** be considered as factor influencing the rate of chemical reaction?
options: The rate constant of the reaction
questions.explanation: The rate constant (k) is a parameter that quantifies the rate of a reaction at a given temperature; it is not an external factor that can be changed directly. Temperature, catalysts, and surface area of reactants are factors that influence the rate by affecting collisions and activation energy.
Step-by-step conceptual review for this question.

questions.questionText: In which of the following order of a reaction, a plot of ln[A]t versus time is a straight line whose slope is -k?
questions.explanation:
For a first-order reaction, the integrated rate law is ln[A]t = ln[A]₀ - kt. Plotting ln[A]t versus time gives a straight line with a slope of -k.

 Zero-order reactions give [A]t versus time as straight lines, and second- and third-order reactions follow different integrated rate laws.

questions.questionText: A forward and reverse reaction continues to take place at equal rate in microscopic level without change in composition at macroscopic level. This statement is the definition of
questions.explanation:
Dynamic equilibrium occurs when the forward and reverse reactions continue at the same rate, so the concentrations of reactants and products remain constant over time at the macroscopic level. 

This is different from the law of mass action, which relates concentrations to the equilibrium constant, and chemical kinetics, which studies the rates of reactions. 

Degree of freedom refers to the number of independent variables in a system.

questions.questionText: What are the four quantum numbers for an electron in a 2s orbital?
questions.explanation:
The four quantum numbers are:

- Principal quantum number (n) = 2 (for the second shell)

- Azimuthal quantum number (l) = 0 (for s-orbital)

- Magnetic quantum number (mₗ) = 0 (since l = 0)

- Spin quantum number (mₛ) = +1/2 (one of the two possible spin states).

questions.questionText: A student uses a digital balance ( 0.02), a thermometer ( 0.1), a measuring cylinder ( 0.05), and a beaker ( 0.5) during an experiment. Which of the above instrument is more precise?
questions.explanation: Precision is indicated by the smallest increment of measurement or the instrument's uncertainty. The instrument with the smallest uncertainty is the most precise:

questions.questionText: Which one of the following explains that light has BOTH wave and particle nature?
options: Microscopic systems, such as atoms and molecules can possess wave properties.
Light consists of electromagnetic waves which have an oscillating electric and magnetic disturbance that spreads electromagnetic radiation.
beam of light is a stream of particles of electromagnetic energy, with energy proportional to the observed frequency of the light.
An electron that is bound to the nucleus behaves like a standing wave and its position is given in terms of probability.
questions.explanation:
The dual nature of light is described by wave-particle duality. 

Light behaves as an electromagnetic wave (oscillating electric and magnetic fields) and also as a stream of particles called photons, each carrying energy E = hν proportional to its frequency.

 The other options describe wave behavior of matter or purely wave characteristics of light.

questions.questionText: A nuclear breakdown in which particles or electromagnetic radiation is emitted is:
questions.explanation:
Radioactive decay is the process by which an unstable atomic nucleus loses energy by emitting particles (alpha, beta) or electromagnetic radiation (gamma rays).

 Radioactivity refers to the general phenomenon, radioactive isotopes are the unstable nuclei themselves, and radio waves are a type of electromagnetic radiation unrelated to nuclear breakdown.

questions.questionText: Which statement describes valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) theory?
options: Atomic orbitals are capable of combining to produce new electron distribution.
covalent bond is formed when orbitals of two atoms overlap and the overlap region is occupied by a pair of electrons.
Each degenerate orbitals are occupied by a single electron before the second electrons of opposite spin enters the orbitals.
Electron pairs will be as far apart from each other in three dimensional spaces as possible.
questions.explanation:
VSEPR theory states that electron pairs around a central atom arrange themselves in 3D space so that they are as far apart as possible to minimize repulsion. 

The other options describe hybridization, covalent bonding (overlap of orbitals), and Hund’s rule for electron filling, which are different concepts.
